messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• On rural roads: 55 mph.
• On city streets: 25–35 mph. | • Exceeding limits can result in fines, points, and possible license suspension. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | • Failure to comply can lead to a $50 fine and points. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | • Violations carry a $50 fine and points. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• For commercial drivers, the limit is 0.04 %.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | • First offense: up to 90 days jail, $1,000 fine. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Stop at stop signs; yield at yield signs.
• At intersections without signs, yield to traffic from the right.
• Pedestrians have priority on crosswalks. | • Failure to yield can result in points and fines. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal before changing lanes.
• Must check mirrors and blind spots.
• Passing on the right is prohibited unless the left lane is occupied. | • Unsafe lane changes can lead to points. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights are only allowed when visibility is ≤ 200 ft. | • Failure to use headlights can result in a $50 fine. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | • Violations can lead to towing and fines. | | **School‑Zone Speed Limits** | • Speed limits drop to 20–25 mph during school hours.
• Violations can result in higher fines and points. | • Enforcement is strict during school days. | | **Points System** | • Accumulating 12 points in 24 months can lead to license suspension.
• Points vary by offense (e.g., 2 points for speeding, 3 for DUI). | • Points are tracked by the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS). | | **Traffic School** | • Eligible drivers can attend a state‑approved traffic school to reduce points. | • Must be completed within 30 days of the ticket. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Vehicles must be registered annually.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | • Failure to register or inspect can lead to fines and impoundment. | | **Special Rules for Commercial Vehicles** | • Commercial drivers must adhere to stricter speed limits and DUI limits.
• Hours‑of‑Service (HOS) regulations apply. | • Violations can lead to license revocation. | **Resources for More Detail** - Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) – Traffic Rules & Regulations - Texas Transportation Code – Chapter 545 (Traffic Rules) - Texas Vehicle Code – Chapter 545 (Vehicle Registration & Inspection) - Texas Highway Patrol – Enforcement Guidelines Feel free to ask if you need specific details on any of these topics!
